text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Cabinet reshuffle delayed, no-confidence fails.
- Foreign Minister Levy considering quitting.
- Shekel settles at 3.5 to the dollar after volatile trading. Central Bank doesn't intervene, dollar up 8.3 percent this year.
- El Al, government clash over size of share offer.
- Prime Minister's office reluctant to cut 600 million shekels more from budget.
- Samsung to open local R&D centre within the year.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Prime Minister Netanyahu struggles to pacify Levy.
- Chief of Staff: Syria improving surprise attack ability.
MAARIV
- Infrastructure Minister Sharon: I'm the only one who can conduct negotiations with Palestinian President Arafat.
- Netanyahu: the true government majority is larger than the no-confidence vote.
- U.S. intelligence planes listen to Israeli army in Lebanon, occupied territories.
- Within two years Iran will have missiles that can hit any place inside Israel.
- Israel to launch new small satellite in September.
HAARETZ
- Likud officials: the coalition's days are numbered.
- Gesher faction will rule in coming days on remaining in coalition; Levy considers resignation.
- Round of appointments will be approved in parliament only on Monday due to Levy, Sharon problems.
- Bank of Israel Governor Frenkel to Sharon: you should pass budget cuts in your first days in the Treasury.
GLOBES
- Dollar representative rate: 3.506 shekels after traded at 3.60.
- Frenkel: Two days ago everyone worried about appreciation; now all are worried about depreciation.
- Treasury weighs tax reforms.
